scenes.heading: Circle properties: angles and chords
scenes.say: Draw any circle, add a few chords, and the angles inside follow neat, reliable rules. Learn them and you can find angles without a protractor.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Every seat on a curved balcony sees the stage at the same angle
scenes.science: Angles on the same arc are equal; the centre sees double
scenes.breaks: Seats on the same side as the stage (the other segment) see a different angle — the two add to 180°.
scenes.say: Picture a stage on the edge of a circular theatre. Every seat on the far side sees the stage at the same angle. A director at the very centre sees it at twice that angle. Seats on the near side see a different angle, though.

scenes.heading: The centre angle is double
notes: Both angles stand on arc AB
scenes.say: First the circle and the points A, B and C. Then the lines from C, making angle theta, and the radii from the centre, making two theta. When both stand on the same arc, the angle at the centre is always double.

scenes.heading: More angle rules
points: Cyclic quad: opposite angles add to 180°
scenes.say: Three more rules. Angles in the same segment are equal. The angle in a semicircle is ninety degrees. And opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add to one hundred and eighty. Also remember two radii make an isosceles triangle.

scenes.heading: Cyclic quadrilateral
scenes.question: ∠A = (3x + 10)°, ∠C = (2x − 5)° are opposite. Find x and ∠A.
scenes.say: Angles A and C are opposite, so they add to one hundred and eighty. That gives five x plus five equals one hundred and eighty, so x is thirty-five, and angle A is one hundred and fifteen degrees.
scenes.caption: (3x + 10) + (2x − 5) = 180, so x = 35 and ∠A = 115°.

scenes.heading: Chords and Pythagoras
scenes.say: Here's a sixteen centimetre chord in a circle of radius ten. The perpendicular from the centre cuts the chord in half, so we get eight. The radius is the hypotenuse: d squared is one hundred minus sixty-four, thirty-six, so d is six centimetres.
scenes.caption: Half-chord 8 cm. d² = 10² − 8² = 36, so d = 6 cm.

points: Perpendicular from O halves a chord
scenes.say: Quick recap. The angle at the centre is double. Angles in the same segment are equal. A semicircle gives ninety degrees. Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add to one hundred and eighty. And the perpendicular from the centre halves a chord. Now try the practice questions!
